correctness.rationale: Cyclic averaging f(omega z) projects any competitor onto degrees divisible by n without increasing its ℓ1 norm; equality in ℓ1 forces all optimal coefficients outside this residue class to vanish. For 0<u<v<1, D_k=uv^k-vu^k>0 and the feasible trinomials F_k=1-P_k t+Q_k t^k attain norm 1+L_k. For a minimizing k, lambda=-(v^k+v)/D_k and mu=(u^k+u)/D_k define h_j=lambda*u^j+mu*v^j with h1=-1, hk=1; feasible F_j for each j≥2 and L_k≤L_j imply h_j≤1. The two-exponential curve h(t) increases then decreases to 0, giving h_j≥-1 for every j≥1, a valid ALL-degree dual certificate rather than a finite enumeration. Equality forces support {1,k}, or {1,k,k+1} at a unique adjacent tie; vanishing equations make the minimizer a trinomial or convex segment. The real extension L(t) has derivative controlled by strictly increasing G(x)=x^(eta+1)+(1+eta)vx-eta*u, proving unique continuous trough and at most adjacent integer minimizers. Direct L2-L3=(u+v+uv-1)/[uv(u+v)] yields first transition, and stationary-root asymptotics give k=log(1/(1-v))/log(1/u)+O_u(1), norm→2/u. Independently evaluated rational samples include exact tie u=1/5,v=2/3 (norm 15), and u=4/5,v=9/10 (index 9). These checks only corroborate the analytic certificate.
